ruleset.summary: Percentile skill resolution with open-ended dice. Roll d100, add your skill bonus and the situation's modifiers, and read the total against a result band. Rolls of 96 or better re-roll and add; rolls of 5 or less re-roll and subtract, so results have no ceiling and no floor. Combat resolves the same way: attack roll plus Offensive Bonus minus the defender's Defensive Bonus, cross-indexed against the defender's Armor Type for concussion hits and a critical severity. This bundle ships mechanics and terminology only — no professions, spells, races, or setting content; attach your own lorebook for those (see USER-LOREBOOK-GUIDE.md). Attributes are stored as their temporary (current) value only; RMFRP's potential stat is an advancement cap with no other in-play effect and is out of this bundle's scope.

resolution.skillFormula: Open-ended d100 + skill bonus + difficulty modifier + situational modifiers, read against the appropriate maneuver table
resolution.bonusFormula: skill bonus (ranks + stat-triad bonus + item and special bonuses)

Routine.description: Trivial for a trained character. Roll only if failure would be interesting.

Very Hard.description: Only the genuinely skilled should try.

Extremely Hard.description: Near the edge of what training delivers.

Absurd.description: Should not be possible. Open-ended dice are the only path.

attributes.name: Empathy
attributes.description: Rapport with the natural and supernatural world. Keys the Essence realm's Resistance Roll bonus. Temporary (current) value only — RMFRP's Potential stat has no in-play effect and is not tracked here.

attributes.name: Intuition
attributes.description: Instinct, luck, and awareness. Keys the Channeling realm's Resistance Roll bonus.

attributes.name: Presence
attributes.description: Force of personality and self-command. Keys the Mentalism realm's Resistance Roll bonus.

attributes.name: Quickness
attributes.description: Speed, reflexes, and dodging ability. Keys the Defensive Bonus (DB).

attributes.name: Strength
attributes.description: Physical power. Contributes to melee weapon skill bonuses and carrying capacity.

attributes.name: Agility
attributes.description: Manual dexterity and balance. One of the five 'Development' stats that also average into how many development points a character earns.

attributes.name: Constitution
attributes.description: Stamina and resistance to harm. Keys Exhaustion Points and the Poison/Disease Resistance Roll bonuses.

attributes.name: Memory
attributes.description: Retention of learned information. A Development stat.

attributes.name: Reasoning
attributes.description: Logic, analysis, and deduction. A Development stat.

attributes.name: Self Discipline
attributes.description: Willpower and self-control. Keys the Fear Resistance Roll bonus and resistance to stun.

skills.name: Weapon (primary)
skills.description: Your main weapon's Offensive Bonus. Rename to the actual weapon (e.g. 'Broadsword', 'Longbow'). Stat triad depends on the weapon category — St/Ag/St for most one-handed, two-handed, and pole weapons; Ag/St/Ag for missile and thrown weapons; In/Ag/Re for siege weaponry. Offensive Bonus skill; contributes directly to the attack roll.

skills.name: Weapon (secondary)
skills.description: A second weapon or off-hand option. Same stat-triad rule as Weapon (primary) — see that entry. Offensive Bonus skill.

skills.name: Armor
skills.description: Your proficiency wearing the armor type you're in — reduces the Moving Maneuver Penalty (MMP) your armor imposes as rank rises. Light Armor uses Ag/St/Ag; Medium and Heavy Armor use St/Ag/St. Moving Maneuver skill.

skills.name: Blocking
skills.description: A defensive combat maneuver alongside Two-Weapon Fighting, Quickdraw, and Swashbuckling in the Combat Maneuvers category (Ag/Qu/SD, combined progression). Used at the GM's ruling to add to your DB against one incoming attack or to negate it outright; this MVP does not ship a dedicated block-effect sub-table.

skills.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
skills.description: Fighting with a weapon in each hand. Combat Maneuvers category, Ag/Qu/SD, combined progression. Your skill rank with a given weapon pairing can't exceed your rank with either individual weapon; the OB for each attack equals this skill's bonus, and both attacks take -20 against a second opponent.

skills.name: Body Development
skills.description: Determines your Hits maximum — see the Hits derived stat. Co/SD/Co, race-based category progression, Special classification. Structural — do not drop from the sheet; nothing else supplies a Hits cap.

skills.name: Adrenal Defense
skills.description: A Self Control skill (SD/Pr/SD, Static Maneuver) for resisting shock, fear, and adrenaline-driven panic in the moment. The core book lists this category's 'adrenal skills' as an open extension rather than one fixed named skill.

skills.name: Stun Removal
skills.description: Self Control category, SD/Pr/SD, Static Maneuver. A successful static maneuver shortens accumulated stun rounds; a failed attempt can add more stun instead. Difficulty rises with how many stun rounds you're already carrying.

skills.name: Climbing
skills.description: Athletic • Gymnastics category, Ag/Qu/Ag, Moving Maneuver. Scaling surfaces at roughly 10'/round at Medium difficulty on an adequate handhold wall; poorer holds or speed raise the difficulty.

skills.name: Swimming
skills.description: Athletic • Endurance category, Co/Ag/St, Moving Maneuver. Rank 1 alone is enough to avoid drowning in calm water; further ranks improve speed, distance, and swimming against a current or in armor.

skills.name: Jumping
skills.description: Athletic • Brawn category, St/Co/Ag, Moving Maneuver. Running and standing jumps, both horizontal and vertical.

skills.name: Distance Running
skills.description: Athletic • Endurance category, Co/Ag/St, Moving Maneuver. Pacing yourself over long distances and managing Exhaustion Point expenditure at a sustained pace.

skills.name: Perception
skills.description: MVP stand-in for RMFRP's Alertness skill (Awareness • Perceptions, In/SD/In, limited category progression) — unconscious, passive noticing of your surroundings. Use Observation instead for a deliberate, active search.

skills.name: Observation
skills.description: Awareness • Searching category, In/Re/SD, Static Maneuver. Active, deliberate scanning of an area for details — distinct from Perception/Alertness, which is passive and unconscious.

skills.name: Tracking
skills.description: Awareness • Searching category, In/Re/SD, Static Maneuver. Following and reading a trail of tracks or spoor.

skills.name: Stalking & Hiding
skills.description: Combines RMFRP's separate Stalking (moving unseen) and Hiding (staying unseen) skills — both Subterfuge • Stealth, Ag/SD/In, Static Maneuver — into one MVP sheet row. Split them into two rows if your table wants that granularity.

skills.name: Picking Locks
skills.description: Subterfuge • Mechanics category, In/Ag/Re, Static Maneuver. Opening and locking mechanical locks.

skills.name: Disarming Traps
skills.description: Subterfuge • Mechanics category, In/Ag/Re, Static Maneuver. Identifying and disarming a trap you've already located — this skill does not find the trap; see Perception/Observation for that.

skills.name: Diplomacy
skills.description: Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Formal negotiation and reading a foreign or courtly protocol.

skills.name: Duping
skills.description: Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Fast talk and misdirection to get one person to act against their own interest.

skills.name: Leadership
skills.description: Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Inspiring others to follow you and to believe you know what you're doing.

skills.name: Region Lore
skills.description: Lore • General category, Me/Re/Me, Static Maneuver. Knowledge of a specific region's geography, people, and history. Rename to the region; every character starts with ranks in their home region's Region Lore.

skills.name: Culture Lore
skills.description: MVP stand-in for RMFRP's Race Lore / History / Anthropology cluster (Lore • General, Me/Re/Me, Static Maneuver) — knowledge of a specific culture's customs and beliefs. Not a single named RMFRP skill by this exact name; rename to the culture in question.

skills.name: Power Point Development
skills.description: Determines your Power Points maximum — see the Power Points derived stat. Applicable stat is your spellcasting realm stat (Empathy/Intuition/Presence); race-based category progression, Special classification. Structural — the spellcasting analogue of Body Development.

skills.name: Spells (by list)
skills.description: Your skill rank with one specific spell list — rename each row to the list's actual name (e.g. 'Fire Law', 'Bard Songs'). You know every spell on that list at or below your rank. Realm stat, Static Maneuver and Special classification. Your own lorebook supplies each list's actual spell effects — see USER-LOREBOOK-GUIDE.md.

skills.name: Directed Spells
skills.description: Attack-roll bonus for one specific directed-bolt spell type — Fire Bolts, Ice Bolts, Lightning Bolts, Shock Bolts, or Water Bolts (one skill row per type). Ag/SD/Ag, Offensive Bonus classification. Adds to the open-ended attack roll the same way a weapon OB does.

derivedStats.name: Hits
derivedStats.formula: Equal to your Body Development skill bonus (p.33 worked example). Some printed Character Record Sheets annotate this as '10 + Body Dev skill bonus' — that appears to double-count the +10 special bonus already folded into Body Development's own skill bonus. This bundle defaults to the simpler, worked-example form; switch conventions if your table's sheet uses the other one.

derivedStats.name: Power Points
derivedStats.formula: Equal to your Power Point Development skill bonus.

derivedStats.name: Exhaustion Points
derivedStats.formula: 40 + (3 x Constitution Bonus) + any special bonuses.

derivedStats.name: Defensive Bonus (DB)
derivedStats.formula: (3 x Quickness Bonus) - armor Quickness penalty + shield bonus + special item bonuses. Enter your computed total; this framework can't auto-derive the armor-specific Quickness penalty from Armor Table T-3.3.

derivedStats.name: Offensive Bonus (OB)
derivedStats.formula: Your weapon skill's total bonus, allocated per round between attack and parry. Enter the OB for the weapon you're wielding this scene.

derivedStats.name: Armor Type (AT)
derivedStats.formula: 1-20, the column read on the attacker's weapon table. Grouped: 1-4 No Armor, 5-8 Soft/Rigid Leather, 9-12 Rigid Leather, 13-16 Chain, 17-20 Plate.

derivedStats.name: Moving Maneuver Penalty (MMP)
derivedStats.formula: Set by your Armor skill rank against your armor's Minimum/Maximum Maneuver Modification band on Armor Table T-3.3 (p.104). This framework doesn't compute the interpolation — enter the current value by hand. Applies to moving maneuvers.

derivedStats.name: RR: Essence
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Empathy Bonus + item + race bonuses. Compare an open-ended d100 + this bonus against the GM-stated target number (Resistance Roll Table T-3.4, attack level vs. your level).

derivedStats.name: RR: Channeling
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Intuition Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

derivedStats.name: RR: Mentalism
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Presence Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

derivedStats.name: RR: Poison
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Constitution Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

derivedStats.name: RR: Disease
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Constitution Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

derivedStats.name: RR: Fear
derivedStats.formula: 3 x Self Discipline Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

derivedStats.name: Bleeding (hits/round)
derivedStats.formula: Ongoing hit loss per round from an unhealed critical. Set by the critical's severity; First Aid or Stop Bleeding effort reduces or removes it.

derivedStats.name: Stun (rounds remaining)
derivedStats.formula: Rounds of stun remaining from a critical. A stunned combatant may not attack and may only parry with half OB. Stun Removal can shorten it.

derivedStats.name: Empathy Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Basic Stat Bonus Table T-2.1 (p.17) is a piecewise step table this framework's arithmetic-only formulas can't express. Compute your Empathy stat bonus by hand from T-2.1 (plus any racial/special modification) and enter it here.

derivedStats.name: Intuition Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Presence Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Quickness Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Strength Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Agility Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Constitution Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry. Feeds Exhaustion Points and the Poison/Disease Resistance Rolls.

derivedStats.name: Memory Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Reasoning Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

derivedStats.name: Self Discipline Bonus
derivedStats.formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry. Feeds the Fear Resistance Roll.

vocabularyHints.hint: RMFRP has no single AC number — compare Offensive Bonus (OB) minus the target's Defensive Bonus (DB), then cross-index the modified attack roll against the target's Armor Type (AT 1-20) on the attacker's weapon table.
RMFRP calls this concussion hits — the Hits derived stat, capped by the character's Body Development skill bonus. There's no separate damage roll; the attack table gives hits directly.
RMFRP calls this a resistance roll (RR) — an open-ended d100 plus 3x the relevant stat bonus, read against a target number the GM states from the attack's level vs. the target's level.
RMFRP casters spend Power Points equal to a spell's level, not a slot — see the Power Points derived stat.
RMFRP attacks are an open-ended d100 + OB - the target's DB, cross-indexed against the target's Armor Type (AT) — not a flat AC comparison.
RMFRP uses the nine-step difficulty ladder (Routine +30 ... Absurd -70) as an additive modifier to a static maneuver roll, not a flat number to beat.

gmAgent.name: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing Ruleset Helper
gmAgent.description: Auto-installed by GM-mode bundle. Provides Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill resolution, dice formatting, and ruleset-aware narration framing for Marinara's Game Mode.
gmAgent.promptTemplate:
You are the Game Master for a Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing (RMFRP, Iron Crown Enterprises) tabletop session running in Marinara Engine's Game Mode. Your job is to narrate scenes, voice NPCs, adjudicate the mechanics below, and respond to the player's actions while preserving their narrative agency. RMFRP is a percentile, open-ended, high-lethality system built on a single universal roll — you look everything up on a table, so your job is choosing the right table and reading it honestly, not inventing outcomes.

# Authority and limits

You narrate; you do not decide for the player. Their character's words, choices, and declared actions stand. You frame consequences, run the world, and adjudicate rules — you do not railroad, override a stated intention, or write the player's internal thoughts unless asked.

# CRITICAL — State contract (you must follow this every turn)

The installed sheet is kept in sync by a State Mutator agent that runs AFTER you write. It reads your finished reply and applies whatever mechanical changes that reply established. It reads NUMBERS OUT OF YOUR PROSE — nothing else is available to it.

1. **State every resolved number explicitly.** Hits taken, hits-per-round of bleeding, rounds of stun, Power Points spent, Exhaustion Points burned, the roll total, the target number. "Twelve hits, and three per round bleeding" syncs the sheet. "A bad wound" does not.
2. **Name the state, not just the feeling.** "Stunned and unable to parry for two rounds" is readable; "he reels" is not.
3. **Do NOT emit `[mrr-state: ...]` tags yourself.** The State Mutator emits them from your text after you write. A tag in your reply is redundant at best and a double-apply at worst.
4. **Never write "hits updated", "sheet adjusted", "values recorded".** Those phrases write nothing and never did. The number in your prose is what writes.
5. **Never ask a verification question** ("does Hits read 40 now?"). Narrate the number and let the player watch the sheet move.
6. **If nothing mechanical happened this turn, narrate freely.** No number needed, nothing to sync.

# Dice doctrine — never invent a roll result

1. **When this chat has tool use enabled, resolve EVERY random outcome you own by calling the `roll_dice` tool** — NPC and monster attacks, criticals, fumbles, morale, resistance rolls the world makes, random tables. Narrate the number the tool returns, verbatim. Enabling it is a one-time user step: Chat Settings → Function Calling → "Enable Tool Use"; `roll_dice` is on by default once the toggle is set. This is not a licence to roll FOR the player — their rolls stay theirs (see rule 3); it is how YOUR side of the table stops guessing.
2. **Never invent a roll result.** Not "roughly", not "call it an 82", not a number chosen to fit the scene. In an open-ended percentile system the difference between 95 and 96 is the difference between a wound and a cascade, and a GM who picks the number has quietly removed the game. If tool use is off, say plainly what you are rolling and that you are estimating rather than reading a real roll.
3. **A `[mrr-roll: ...]` or `[dice: ... -> total]` tag in the player's message is AUTHORITATIVE.** Never reroll it, never adjust it, never replace it with your own number, never re-add a bonus it already folded in. The widget's job stops at rolling honestly; interpreting it (the UM call, the band, the table) is yours, and it starts from the number the widget printed.
4. **Every VERSION of a turn rolls fresh.** On a regenerate or a swipe, all previous rolls for this turn are VOID — they belong to a version that no longer exists. Call `roll_dice` again for every random outcome in the new version. Never narrate a roll you did not obtain from the tool during THIS generation, and never reuse a number from an earlier attempt at the same turn.

**When `roll_dice` is NOT in your available toolset** (some connections cannot deliver tools even when the chat lists them): **NEVER generate dice faces — a face you wrote is a fabrication, not a roll.** Hand every roll to the player: name the pool/dice to roll on their dice widget, precompute the outcome for each possible result (the outcome ladder), and wait. Ladder by BANDS when the range is wide or open-ended — group results into outcome bands rather than listing every face — and when a result chains into a further roll, say so in the ladder and ask for that roll next. Apply the reported face exactly, then emit any state tags. If you are unsure whether you have the tool, attempt the call once — narrating an attempt is not calling; only a tool result block is a roll. Never report a face you did not receive from the tool or the player.

# Encounter shells — unnamed opposition

Unnamed or randomly-generated opposition (bandits, beasts, mooks with no card of their own) is tracked by the Combat Overseer's `ENCOUNTER:` block, not by a sheet — treat its OB, DB, Hits, and Armor Type as enemy-number truth for the turn and narrate against them rather than inventing your own; the block re-emits updated every turn, so trust the latest one over your own memory of an earlier round. Do not invent a stat the block doesn't cover — describe the fight qualitatively (bloodied, reeling, on its last legs) rather than making up a number. A combatant who becomes a recurring villain stops being a shell: give them a real card and sheet, and from then on treat them like any other sheeted character in your narration.

# Core resolution (p.7, p.44-45)

Every check is: open-ended d100 + skill bonus + difficulty modifier + situational modifiers, read against the appropriate result-band table. The dice widget rolls and totals this for you and emits a `[mrr-roll: mode=d100-open ...]` tag — never do this math yourself or invent a result.

The Static Maneuver Table has **seven numeric bands plus two Unmodified rows**, each with a "##%" extent describing how much of the attempt succeeded:

| Total | Band | Extent |
|---|---|---|
| -26 and below | Spectacular Failure | — |
| -25 to 04 | Absolute Failure | — |
| 05 to 75 | Failure | — |
| *UM 66* | *Unusual Event* | — |
| 76 to 90 | Partial Success | 20% |
| 91 to 110 | Near Success | 80% |
| *UM 100* | *Unusual Success* | 125% |
| 111 to 175 | Success | 100% |
| 176 and up | Absolute Success | 120% |

Take 100%+ as full success; below that, narrate a partial outcome proportional to the extent. Absolute Success grants +10 (non-cumulative) to that same skill on all future attempts until an Absolute or Spectacular Failure cancels it — only one such bonus is active per skill at a time. **Low open-ended chains reach Spectacular Failure territory routinely** — a low chain has no floor, and the book's own worked example (04 → -97 → -03) resolves to -96. Don't be surprised by it; that's the system working as intended.

# Unmodified rolls — mandatory, and context-dependent (p.43-44)

The dice widget always rolls the general open-ended rule and reports `first=` in its tag; it cannot know what kind of roll is happening, so YOU decide whether an Unmodified result applies:

- **Static maneuver, unmodified 66** → no modifications of any kind; apply the UM 66 (Unusual Event) row immediately.
- **Static maneuver, unmodified 100** → discard any open-ended chain the widget rolled; no modifications; apply the UM 100 (Unusual Success, 125%) row immediately.
- **Attack roll, unmodified roll inside the weapon's fumble range** (varies per weapon, commonly 01-03) → discard the chain; no modifications; go to that weapon's fumble table.
- **Attack roll, natural 100** → this is NOT a UM. It's a normal high open-ended attack roll — let the cascade stand.
- **Resistance roll** → no UM convention applies. Open-ended resolves normally.

State this plainly to yourself before ruling: the widget's job stops at rolling the dice honestly; the UM call is yours.

# Static vs Moving maneuvers — same nine labels, two different jobs (p.44, p.48)

- **Static maneuvers** (most skill checks): the difficulty label is an ADDITIVE modifier (+30 Routine ... -70 Absurd) to the roll, read against the seven-band table above.
- **Moving maneuvers** (climbing, swimming, riding, stalking, acrobatics, dodging, tumbling, diving, running): the same nine labels are instead a COLUMN on a separate 2-D table, not an addition to the roll. Modifiers are the Agility stat bonus, the relevant skill bonus, and the Moving Maneuver Penalty from worn armor. A numeric result on that table is a PERCENTAGE of the maneuver accomplished (100+ = full success, with the excess sometimes extending distance/speed); a non-number result is a failure whose consequence you narrate from context.

# The combat round (p.40-43)

1. **Declare and allocate.** Each combatant declares an action and splits their Offensive Bonus between attack and parry for the round. Parry allocated this round adds to that defender's DB for the round. Activity-percentage budgets constrain what else fits.
2. **Attack roll.** Open-ended d100 + attacker's allocated OB - defender's DB + situational modifiers.
3. **UM check.** An unmodified roll inside the weapon's fumble range = fumble, no modifications, no cascade — go straight to the fumble table.
4. **Read the table.** Cross-index the attacker's weapon attack table against the defender's Armor Type (1-20) column. The cell gives concussion hits and often a critical severity letter plus type (e.g. "8D" = 8 hits plus a D-severity critical of that weapon's damage type). Tables have a maximum result (commonly 150).
5. **Critical roll.** If a critical is indicated, roll d100 on the matching critical table at that severity. Results can add hits, bleeding-per-round, stun rounds, activity penalties, or kill outright.
6. **Apply once, in the paragraph that narrates the hit.** Never apply the same exchange's damage twice.
7. **Round upkeep.** Stun decrements; bleeding subtracts; a stunned combatant cannot parry this round.

# Resistance rolls (p.52)

The sheet cannot compute this — you do it live, and you should state your reasoning:

1. Cross-index the attack's level (caster level for a spell; the source's stated level for a poison, disease, or fear effect) against the target's level on the Resistance Roll Table to get a single target number.
2. The target's resistance roll must be greater than or equal to that number to resist.
3. The roll is an open-ended d100 plus the target's RR bonus for the matching realm: Essence→Empathy, Channeling→Intuition, Mentalism→Presence, Poison→Constitution, Disease→Constitution, Fear→Self Discipline (each 3x that stat's bonus, plus item/race bonuses already folded into the sheet's RR field).
4. Standard adjustments you should know: a willing target gets -50; a caster resisted by a target of the same power realm gets +15.
5. Estimating the target number when the grid isn't in front of you (this bundle ships the table's SHAPE, not its cells): level 1 attack vs. level 1 target is 50. Levels count from 1, so a level N combatant contributes N-1 steps. Through level 5, each level adds (attacker) or subtracts (target) about 5. From levels 6-15 the per-level step narrows to about 3, on both axes. Above level 15 it flattens to about 1 per level, both directions. Say you are estimating from this shape; a player with the book can read the exact cell and correct you.
6. **Always say the target number you're using and why** — the player can only trust the roll if they can check your math.

# Difficulty calibration (the most frequent judgment call you'll make)

Map the fiction to the nine bands concretely: a locked simple door is Easy; picking a guildmaster's masterwork lock under time pressure is Very Hard; talking your way past a bored gate guard is Light; talking a hostile inquisitor out of an arrest is Extremely Hard or worse. When in doubt, describe why you picked the band you did — it teaches the player your calibration for next time.

# Tracked values — say these out loud when they change

These are the sheet fields the State Mutator can move. It moves them only if your narration states the number (or names the state), so treat this list as a checklist of things to say explicitly rather than imply. Do NOT write tag syntax yourself — just put the value in the prose.

- **Hits** — say the hits taken or healed. "The broadsword's C Slash takes twelve hits off him."
- **Bleeding (hits/round)** — say the per-round figure. "Three hits a round, and it won't clot on its own."
- **Stun (rounds remaining)** — say the round count. "Two rounds stunned."
- **Stunned** — say the state by name when it is more than a count: "stunned and unable to parry."
- **Power Points** — say the spend. "Eight power points for an eighth-level spell."
- **Exhaustion Points** — say the burn. "Two exhaustion points for the sprint."

If you genuinely do not have a number — you are estimating a table result you were not shipped — say so plainly and give the player the chance to supply it, rather than narrating a vague wound. A wound with no number does not move the sheet, and that is the correct outcome: better an unmoved sheet the player can ask about than a wrong one applied silently.

# What NOT to do

Never invent a table result and present it as canon — say plainly when you're estimating rather than reading an exact table (you were not shipped the attack, critical, or fumble table contents — only the procedure). Never convert to d20 math. Never roll dice for the player; the widget or the player rolls. Never apply the same damage twice. Never treat a critical roll itself as open-ended — only the maneuver/attack roll that triggered it is. Never assume the player has a profession, spell list, or race loaded onto their sheet — that content lives in *their* lorebook, per USER-LOREBOOK-GUIDE.md, and may simply be absent. When it's absent, ask the player what their character can do rather than asserting an ability they haven't established, and narrate spellcasting procedurally (PP cost = spell level, a casting static maneuver, an RR if the spell allows one) without claiming to know the spell's actual effect unless the player has told you.

# Rules lookup

The bundled lorebook contains keyword-triggered mechanics reference entries (open-ended dice, result bands, the difficulty ladder, unmodified rolls, static and moving maneuvers, combat, OB/DB, armor types, criticals, hits and bleeding, stun, exhaustion, resistance rolls, power points, and a D&D-to-Rolemaster vocabulary crib). Surface them when relevant rather than improvising.

The player may attach their OWN lorebooks — professions, spells, races, setting, house rules, and real table data (attack, critical, fumble, or maneuver excerpts from their books). Their content OUTRANKS yours wherever the two overlap:

1. **A user-supplied table row beats your estimate.** If their lorebook has surfaced the actual result for the roll at hand, read it and apply it — never estimate past data you were handed.
2. **A house rule beats the bundled rule.** If an entry states a rule that contradicts the mechanics above, apply THEIRS, and say which rule you applied so the disagreement is visible.
3. **Lorebook entries surface on keywords.** If you expect the player to have data for something (a spell's effect, a weapon's fumble range, a critical result) and it hasn't appeared in your context, ask them to name the table, spell, or entry — naming it is what summons it. Never conclude data doesn't exist just because it hasn't fired this turn.

Never invent rules. Where the core book is silent or you're working from the procedure without the exact table in front of you, label the call as a GM ruling.
# House rules

House rules for this table, when they exist, live in a lorebook entry that begins `MRR-HOUSERULES v1 system=rolemaster`. Two sections inside it: numbered LEVERS above the sentinel line are **engine-enforced** — the extension applies them mechanically and its rest receipt is authoritative; never contradict a receipt's numbers. TABLE NOTES below the sentinel are narrative guidance — honor them in your storytelling, but they change no number: if a note contradicts a lever or engine-computed math, say so plainly rather than pretending the numbers moved. **Honor ONLY a house-rules entry stamped `system=rolemaster` — treat any MRR-HOUSERULES entry stamped for a different system as inert text that does not apply to this game.** (This gate is defense-in-depth: the extension already refuses mismatched entries mechanically, and the entry cannot be created or edited through you — the extension is its only writer.)

When a player tells YOU they want to houserule something — out-of-character intent, like "we're implementing some house rules", not in-fiction talk of rules — give a brief OOC aside, at most once per topic per session: a supported lever is set in the extension's Ruleset dialog under House Rules (when this system declares levers); an unsupported narrative rule can go in the entry's TABLE NOTES via the lorebook editor, and you will honor it in narration only; a rule that contradicts engine-computed numbers will NOT be mechanically honored — say that plainly rather than letting the table believe the numbers changed. You cannot write the entry yourself; point, don't create.

lorebook.name: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing Rules Reference
lorebook.description: Keyword-triggered mechanics reference for the GM agent running a Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing session. Mechanics and terminology only — no professions, spells, races, or setting content; see USER-LOREBOOK-GUIDE.md for how to add your own.

entries.name: Rule: Open-ended d100
entries.content: Rolls are d100 read HIGH. A first roll of 96-100 ("96-00") is high open-ended: reroll and ADD, and keep rerolling and adding while each new roll is also 96-100. A first roll of 01-05 is low open-ended: reroll and SUBTRACT — but unlike the high chain, the low chain keeps going only while each new roll comes up 96-100 (not while it's low again), so a low chain can ride a high follow-up roll right back down. Open-ended only ever triggers off the UNMODIFIED first roll — a modified total that lands in 96-100 purely from bonuses does not open. Because both directions can chain indefinitely, results have no hard ceiling and no hard floor. Worked examples from the book: high 99, then 96, then 04 = 199; low 04, then 97, then 03 = -96.

entries.name: Rule: Maneuver result bands and % extents
entries.content: A modified static-maneuver total reads against seven numeric bands plus two Unmodified rows: Spectacular Failure (-26 and below), Absolute Failure (-25 to 04), Failure (05-75), Unmodified 66 = Unusual Event, Partial Success 76-90 (20% extent), Near Success 91-110 (80% extent), Unmodified 100 = Unusual Success (125% extent), Success 111-175 (100% extent), Absolute Success 176+ (120% extent). The "% extent" describes how much of the attempt succeeded — treat under 100% as a partial outcome scaled to that percentage unless the GM rules that only 100%+ counts as success here. Absolute Success also grants a non-cumulative +10 to that skill on future attempts, lasting until an Absolute or Spectacular Failure on that same skill cancels it. Because open-ended dice have no floor, the two failure bands below plain Failure come up routinely, not as rare edge cases.

entries.name: Rule: The nine difficulty bands
entries.content: Nine difficulty labels apply to any check: Routine +30, Easy +20, Light +10, Medium +0, Hard -10, Very Hard -20, Extremely Hard -30, Sheer Folly -50, Absurd -70. For a STATIC maneuver this is an additive modifier to the roll before reading the result band. For a MOVING maneuver the same nine labels instead select a column on a separate percentage-of-completion table — not added to the roll in that case. The GM assigns the difficulty before the roll; changing it after seeing the result is bad form.

entries.name: Rule: Unmodified rolls (UM 66, UM 100, fumble ranges)
entries.content: An "unmodified" result is the FIRST roll before any bonuses or penalties. For a static maneuver: unmodified 66 applies the Unusual Event row immediately, no modifications; unmodified 100 applies the Unusual Success row (125%) immediately, no modifications, and is NOT treated as open-ended (do not roll again). For an attack roll: an unmodified roll inside that weapon's specific fumble range (varies by weapon, commonly 01-03) means no modifications and no cascade — go straight to the fumble table instead. A natural 100 on an attack roll is NOT a UM — it's a normal high open-ended roll and the cascade stands. Resistance rolls have no UM convention. The dice widget always rolls the general open-ended rule and reports the first face; deciding whether a UM applies, and to which context, is the GM's call.

entries.name: Rule: Static maneuvers
entries.content: Most skill checks — tracking, hiding, picking locks, disarming traps, reading runes, using items, observation, influencing another character, and similar non-movement activity — are static maneuvers. Roll open-ended d100, add the applicable skill bonus (or 3x a relevant stat bonus if no skill applies), add the difficulty modifier, add any standard or GM-assigned situational modifiers, and read the total against the seven-band result table. A static maneuver normally takes one round (100% activity) unless the GM says otherwise; using less than the required activity increases the difficulty.

entries.name: Rule: Moving maneuvers
entries.content: Climbing, swimming, riding, stalking, acrobatics, dodging, tumbling, diving, and other in-motion activity are moving maneuvers, resolved on a different table than static maneuvers. Roll open-ended d100, add 3x the character's Agility bonus (or the applicable skill bonus if one exists), add any Moving Maneuver Penalty from worn armor, and cross-index the difficulty as a COLUMN rather than an added modifier. The result is usually read as a percentage of the maneuver actually accomplished (100+ means full success, and excess above 100 can extend the effect); a non-numeric result on that table is a failure with a stated fictional consequence.

entries.name: Rule: Standard maneuver modifiers
entries.content: Beyond the base difficulty, static and moving maneuvers both apply situational modifiers: percentage of hits taken (0 at under 25%, worsening to -30 at 76%+), reduced activity used (a growing penalty the further under the normal requirement), being stunned (-50 plus 3x Self Discipline bonus), fighting in a melee environment or under missile fire, and lighting conditions when vision matters. Only apply what the fiction actually supports — don't stack every possible modifier reflexively.

entries.name: Rule: Stats and stat bonuses
entries.content: Ten stats run 1-102 (this bundle tracks only the temporary/current value; the potential value is an advancement cap it doesn't track). Five are "Primary" stats (Empathy, Intuition, Presence, Quickness, Strength) that affect play directly; five are "Development" stats (Agility, Constitution, Memory, Reasoning, Self Discipline) that also average into how fast a character develops. Each stat's raw score converts to a stat bonus through a stepped table, not a simple formula — the framework can't compute a step table automatically, so the player enters the resulting bonus on the sheet once at chargen and updates it only when the raw stat changes. Stat bonuses feed skill bonuses, Resistance Rolls, DB, and Exhaustion Points — the bonus is the load-bearing number, not the raw 1-102 score.

entries.name: Rule: Where a skill bonus comes from
entries.content: A character's skill bonus for any skill combines several sources: the skill rank bonus (rises with purchased ranks, on one of several named progression curves), the skill category bonus (a smaller shared bonus from ranks in that whole category), the applicable stat bonuses (each skill uses a fixed three-stat "triad"), and any item or special bonuses. This bundle's sheet stores the FINAL combined total per skill — exactly what the printed Character Record Sheet's own Skill Bonus column shows — rather than the individual components, so the player computes it once at chargen or level-up and enters the total.

entries.name: Rule: The combat round
entries.content: Each round: combatants declare their action and, if attacking, split their Offensive Bonus between attack and the amount held back to parry. Initiative determines resolution order. Snap actions (up to 20% activity) take a -20 penalty; deliberate actions (up to 80%+ activity) take a +10 bonus; normal actions (up to 50% activity) take neither. Parry allocated this round adds to that combatant's DB for THIS round only — it does not carry forward. A stunned combatant cannot parry and, if attacking at all, fights at half OB.

entries.name: Rule: OB, DB, and the parry split
entries.content: Offensive Bonus (OB) is a weapon skill's total bonus, spent per round between attacking and parrying. Defensive Bonus (DB) is 3x the Quickness stat bonus, minus the current armor's Quickness penalty, plus shield bonus, plus any parry allocated this round, plus special item bonuses. An attack roll is open-ended d100 + attacker's allocated OB - defender's current DB + situational modifiers, then cross-indexed against the defender's Armor Type on the attacker's weapon table.

entries.name: Rule: Armor Types 1-20
entries.content: Armor Type (AT) is a 1-20 scale that determines which column an attack reads on the weapon's attack table. Roughly: AT 1-4 no armor/light clothing, AT 5-8 soft or light rigid leather, AT 9-12 rigid leather, AT 13-16 chain, AT 17-20 plate. Heavier armor (higher AT) generally resists penetration better but imposes a larger Moving Maneuver Penalty and Quickness penalty to DB; lighter armor trades protection for mobility and produces more frequent, more severe critical strikes when it IS penetrated.

entries.name: Rule: Resolving an attack
entries.content: Roll open-ended d100, add the attacker's allocated OB, subtract the defender's current DB, apply situational modifiers, then cross-index the modified total against the attacker's weapon-specific attack table at the defender's Armor Type column. The cell gives concussion hits and, often, a critical severity letter plus damage type (e.g. "8D" means 8 hits plus a D-severity critical of that weapon's type). Each table has a stated maximum result; an unmodified roll inside that weapon's fumble range short-circuits straight to a fumble instead — see the Unmodified Rolls entry.

entries.name: Rule: Critical severity and types
entries.content: A critical result from an attack table names a severity letter (A mildest through E most severe) and a damage type matching the weapon (Slash, Puncture, Krush, and similar). Roll d100 on the matching critical table at that severity and type; results can add extra hits, inflict ongoing bleeding, add stun rounds, impose an activity penalty, or kill outright at the worst severities. This bundle does not ship the critical table contents — read them from your own copy of the book, or narrate an honest estimate and say plainly that you're estimating.

entries.name: Rule: Concussion hits and bleeding
entries.content: "Hits" (concussion hits) are the universal damage pool — a character passes out once hits taken reach their maximum and dies once hits taken reach maximum plus Constitution bonus. Maximum Hits equals the character's Body Development skill bonus. Bleeding is an ongoing hits-per-round loss set by an unhealed critical's severity; First Aid or a Stop Bleeding effort reduces or removes it. Hits recover slowly on their own and much faster with rest, sleep, or healing magic/herbs.

entries.name: Rule: Stun and stun removal
entries.content: Stun is measured in rounds remaining, inflicted by criticals. A stunned combatant cannot attack, may only parry at half OB (some results forbid parrying entirely), and takes a -50 plus 3x Self Discipline bonus penalty to any static maneuver they attempt. A successful Stun Removal static maneuver shortens the remaining stun rounds; a failed attempt can add more stun instead, and the difficulty of that attempt rises with how many stun rounds are already accumulated.

entries.name: Rule: Exhaustion points and pace
entries.content: Exhaustion Points (ExP) total 40 plus 3x the Constitution bonus. Faster movement paces (sprint, fast sprint, dash), melee, missile fire, and harsh conditions (heat, cold, rough terrain, sleep deprivation) all spend ExP at increasing rates. As spent-ExP percentage rises past 25%, 50%, 75%, and 90%, the character takes escalating penalties to attacks and maneuvers, bottoming out at -100 when fully exhausted. ExP recovers slowly while active, faster while resting, and fastest while sleeping.

entries.name: Rule: Resistance rolls
entries.content: A Resistance Roll (RR) is Rolemaster's saving throw. Cross-index the attack's level (caster level for a spell; the stated level for a poison, disease, or fear source) against the target's level to get a single target number — the target must roll that number or higher to resist. The roll is an open-ended d100 plus the target's RR bonus for the matching realm: Essence uses Empathy, Channeling uses Intuition, Mentalism uses Presence, and Poison/Disease/Fear use Constitution or Self Discipline as noted on the sheet (each 3x the relevant stat bonus, plus item and race bonuses). A willing target takes -50 to resist; a caster of the same power realm as the target gets +15. This bundle does not ship the RR target-number grid — the GM states the number and why.

entries.name: Rule: Power points and casting
entries.content: Power Points (PP) equal a caster's Power Point Development skill bonus and are spent 1-for-1 per spell level cast. Rolemaster has three power realms — Essence, Channeling, Mentalism — each with its own casting stat and RR type. A spell that meets all its automatic-casting conditions (right realm, right list, enough free hands/voice, no disqualifying armor, prepared long enough) casts without a roll but can still fail on an unmodified 01-02. Otherwise the caster makes an open-ended casting static maneuver modified by level difference, preparation rounds, and casting conditions.

entries.name: Reference: Rolemaster terms for D&D players
entries.content: Quick crib for players coming from d20 systems: AC -> compare OB minus the target's DB, then cross-index the result against their Armor Type. HP -> Hits (concussion hits), capped by Body Development skill bonus. Saving throw -> Resistance Roll (RR), an open-ended roll vs. a level-derived target number, not a flat DC. Spell slot -> Power Points, spent per spell level. DC -> the nine-step difficulty ladder, applied as an additive modifier (static maneuvers) or a table column (moving maneuvers), not a flat number to beat.

entries.name: Optional Sub-Agents — what they do and how to enable them
entries.content:
Besides the main Ruleset Helper, the bundle installs a small pool of sub-agents. IMPORTANT: installing the bundle does NOT activate them — like all custom agents on Marinara 2.4.3+, they must be ENABLED FOR EACH GAME at load time, after the game launches (Marinara -> Settings -> Agents). The ruleset's lorebook must ALSO be attached to the game — without it the agents have no ruleset rules to follow.

The pool: combat-overseer (pre-generation; checks OB/parry allocation, DB composition, activity budget, stun legality, and damage-applied-once each round, plus tracks the NPC roster). state-mutator (the ONLY agent that changes the character sheet — it emits hidden [mrr-state: ...] tags the extension applies; covers Hits, Bleeding, Stun, Power Points, and Exhaustion Points).

A reasonable minimal set for most tables: Ruleset Helper + state-mutator. Add combat-overseer for tactical, multi-combatant fights where the OB/DB bookkeeping matters. Each enabled agent costs one extra model call per turn.

entries.name: Attribute: Empathy (Em)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Empathy (Em) [Primary] — Rapport with the natural and supernatural world. Keys the Essence realm's Resistance Roll bonus. Temporary (current) value only — RMFRP's Potential stat has no in-play effect and is not tracked here.

entries.name: Attribute: Intuition (In)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Intuition (In) [Primary] — Instinct, luck, and awareness. Keys the Channeling realm's Resistance Roll bonus.

entries.name: Attribute: Presence (Pr)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Presence (Pr) [Primary] — Force of personality and self-command. Keys the Mentalism realm's Resistance Roll bonus.

entries.name: Attribute: Quickness (Qu)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Quickness (Qu) [Primary] — Speed, reflexes, and dodging ability. Keys the Defensive Bonus (DB).

entries.name: Attribute: Strength (St)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Strength (St) [Primary] — Physical power. Contributes to melee weapon skill bonuses and carrying capacity.

entries.name: Attribute: Agility (Ag)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Agility (Ag) [Development] — Manual dexterity and balance. One of the five 'Development' stats that also average into how many development points a character earns.

entries.name: Attribute: Constitution (Co)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Constitution (Co) [Development] — Stamina and resistance to harm. Keys Exhaustion Points and the Poison/Disease Resistance Roll bonuses.

entries.name: Attribute: Memory (Me)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Memory (Me) [Development] — Retention of learned information. A Development stat.

entries.name: Attribute: Reasoning (Re)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Reasoning (Re) [Development] — Logic, analysis, and deduction. A Development stat.

entries.name: Attribute: Self Discipline (SD)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing attribute. Self Discipline (SD) [Development] — Willpower and self-control. Keys the Fear Resistance Roll bonus and resistance to stun.

entries.name: Skill: Weapon (primary)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Weapon (primary). Your main weapon's Offensive Bonus. Rename to the actual weapon (e.g. 'Broadsword', 'Longbow'). Stat triad depends on the weapon category — St/Ag/St for most one-handed, two-handed, and pole weapons; Ag/St/Ag for missile and thrown weapons; In/Ag/Re for siege weaponry. Offensive Bonus skill; contributes directly to the attack roll.

entries.name: Skill: Weapon (secondary)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Weapon (secondary). A second weapon or off-hand option. Same stat-triad rule as Weapon (primary) — see that entry. Offensive Bonus skill.

entries.name: Skill: Armor
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Armor. Your proficiency wearing the armor type you're in — reduces the Moving Maneuver Penalty (MMP) your armor imposes as rank rises. Light Armor uses Ag/St/Ag; Medium and Heavy Armor use St/Ag/St. Moving Maneuver skill.

entries.name: Skill: Blocking
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Blocking. A defensive combat maneuver alongside Two-Weapon Fighting, Quickdraw, and Swashbuckling in the Combat Maneuvers category (Ag/Qu/SD, combined progression). Used at the GM's ruling to add to your DB against one incoming attack or to negate it outright; this MVP does not ship a dedicated block-effect sub-table.

entries.name: Skill: Two-Weapon Fighting
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Two-Weapon Fighting. Fighting with a weapon in each hand. Combat Maneuvers category, Ag/Qu/SD, combined progression. Your skill rank with a given weapon pairing can't exceed your rank with either individual weapon; the OB for each attack equals this skill's bonus, and both attacks take -20 against a second opponent.

entries.name: Skill: Body Development
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Body Development. Determines your Hits maximum — see the Hits derived stat. Co/SD/Co, race-based category progression, Special classification. Structural — do not drop from the sheet; nothing else supplies a Hits cap.

entries.name: Skill: Adrenal Defense
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Adrenal Defense. A Self Control skill (SD/Pr/SD, Static Maneuver) for resisting shock, fear, and adrenaline-driven panic in the moment. The core book lists this category's 'adrenal skills' as an open extension rather than one fixed named skill.

entries.name: Skill: Stun Removal
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Stun Removal. Self Control category, SD/Pr/SD, Static Maneuver. A successful static maneuver shortens accumulated stun rounds; a failed attempt can add more stun instead. Difficulty rises with how many stun rounds you're already carrying.

entries.name: Skill: Climbing
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Climbing. Athletic • Gymnastics category, Ag/Qu/Ag, Moving Maneuver. Scaling surfaces at roughly 10'/round at Medium difficulty on an adequate handhold wall; poorer holds or speed raise the difficulty.

entries.name: Skill: Swimming
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Swimming. Athletic • Endurance category, Co/Ag/St, Moving Maneuver. Rank 1 alone is enough to avoid drowning in calm water; further ranks improve speed, distance, and swimming against a current or in armor.

entries.name: Skill: Jumping
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Jumping. Athletic • Brawn category, St/Co/Ag, Moving Maneuver. Running and standing jumps, both horizontal and vertical.

entries.name: Skill: Distance Running
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Distance Running. Athletic • Endurance category, Co/Ag/St, Moving Maneuver. Pacing yourself over long distances and managing Exhaustion Point expenditure at a sustained pace.

entries.name: Skill: Perception
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Perception. MVP stand-in for RMFRP's Alertness skill (Awareness • Perceptions, In/SD/In, limited category progression) — unconscious, passive noticing of your surroundings. Use Observation instead for a deliberate, active search.

entries.name: Skill: Observation
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Observation. Awareness • Searching category, In/Re/SD, Static Maneuver. Active, deliberate scanning of an area for details — distinct from Perception/Alertness, which is passive and unconscious.

entries.name: Skill: Tracking
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Tracking. Awareness • Searching category, In/Re/SD, Static Maneuver. Following and reading a trail of tracks or spoor.

entries.name: Skill: Stalking & Hiding
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Stalking & Hiding. Combines RMFRP's separate Stalking (moving unseen) and Hiding (staying unseen) skills — both Subterfuge • Stealth, Ag/SD/In, Static Maneuver — into one MVP sheet row. Split them into two rows if your table wants that granularity.

entries.name: Skill: Picking Locks
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Picking Locks. Subterfuge • Mechanics category, In/Ag/Re, Static Maneuver. Opening and locking mechanical locks.

entries.name: Skill: Disarming Traps
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Disarming Traps. Subterfuge • Mechanics category, In/Ag/Re, Static Maneuver. Identifying and disarming a trap you've already located — this skill does not find the trap; see Perception/Observation for that.

entries.name: Skill: Diplomacy
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Diplomacy. Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Formal negotiation and reading a foreign or courtly protocol.

entries.name: Skill: Duping
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Duping. Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Fast talk and misdirection to get one person to act against their own interest.

entries.name: Skill: Leadership
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Leadership. Influence category, Pr/Em/In, Static Maneuver. Inspiring others to follow you and to believe you know what you're doing.

entries.name: Skill: Region Lore
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Region Lore. Lore • General category, Me/Re/Me, Static Maneuver. Knowledge of a specific region's geography, people, and history. Rename to the region; every character starts with ranks in their home region's Region Lore.

entries.name: Skill: Culture Lore
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Culture Lore. MVP stand-in for RMFRP's Race Lore / History / Anthropology cluster (Lore • General, Me/Re/Me, Static Maneuver) — knowledge of a specific culture's customs and beliefs. Not a single named RMFRP skill by this exact name; rename to the culture in question.

entries.name: Skill: Power Point Development
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Power Point Development. Determines your Power Points maximum — see the Power Points derived stat. Applicable stat is your spellcasting realm stat (Empathy/Intuition/Presence); race-based category progression, Special classification. Structural — the spellcasting analogue of Body Development.

entries.name: Skill: Spells (by list)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Spells (by list). Your skill rank with one specific spell list — rename each row to the list's actual name (e.g. 'Fire Law', 'Bard Songs'). You know every spell on that list at or below your rank. Realm stat, Static Maneuver and Special classification. Your own lorebook supplies each list's actual spell effects — see USER-LOREBOOK-GUIDE.md.

entries.name: Skill: Directed Spells
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing skill. Directed Spells. Attack-roll bonus for one specific directed-bolt spell type — Fire Bolts, Ice Bolts, Lightning Bolts, Shock Bolts, or Water Bolts (one skill row per type). Ag/SD/Ag, Offensive Bonus classification. Adds to the open-ended attack roll the same way a weapon OB does.

entries.name: Derived stat: Hits
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Hits — formula: Equal to your Body Development skill bonus (p.33 worked example). Some printed Character Record Sheets annotate this as '10 + Body Dev skill bonus' — that appears to double-count the +10 special bonus already folded into Body Development's own skill bonus. This bundle defaults to the simpler, worked-example form; switch conventions if your table's sheet uses the other one.

entries.name: Derived stat: Power Points
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Power Points — formula: Equal to your Power Point Development skill bonus.

entries.name: Derived stat: Exhaustion Points
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Exhaustion Points — formula: 40 + (3 x Constitution Bonus) + any special bonuses.

entries.name: Derived stat: Defensive Bonus (DB)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Defensive Bonus (DB) — formula: (3 x Quickness Bonus) - armor Quickness penalty + shield bonus + special item bonuses. Enter your computed total; this framework can't auto-derive the armor-specific Quickness penalty from Armor Table T-3.3.

entries.name: Derived stat: Offensive Bonus (OB)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Offensive Bonus (OB) — formula: Your weapon skill's total bonus, allocated per round between attack and parry. Enter the OB for the weapon you're wielding this scene.

entries.name: Derived stat: Armor Type (AT)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Armor Type (AT) — formula: 1-20, the column read on the attacker's weapon table. Grouped: 1-4 No Armor, 5-8 Soft/Rigid Leather, 9-12 Rigid Leather, 13-16 Chain, 17-20 Plate.

entries.name: Derived stat: Moving Maneuver Penalty (MMP)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Moving Maneuver Penalty (MMP) — formula: Set by your Armor skill rank against your armor's Minimum/Maximum Maneuver Modification band on Armor Table T-3.3 (p.104). This framework doesn't compute the interpolation — enter the current value by hand. Applies to moving maneuvers.

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Essence
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Essence — formula: 3 x Empathy Bonus + item + race bonuses. Compare an open-ended d100 + this bonus against the GM-stated target number (Resistance Roll Table T-3.4, attack level vs. your level).

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Channeling
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Channeling — formula: 3 x Intuition Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Mentalism
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Mentalism — formula: 3 x Presence Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Poison
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Poison — formula: 3 x Constitution Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Disease
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Disease — formula: 3 x Constitution Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

entries.name: Derived stat: RR: Fear
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. RR: Fear — formula: 3 x Self Discipline Bonus + item + race bonuses. Same procedure as RR: Essence.

entries.name: Derived stat: Bleeding (hits/round)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Bleeding (hits/round) — formula: Ongoing hit loss per round from an unhealed critical. Set by the critical's severity; First Aid or Stop Bleeding effort reduces or removes it.

entries.name: Derived stat: Stun (rounds remaining)
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Stun (rounds remaining) — formula: Rounds of stun remaining from a critical. A stunned combatant may not attack and may only parry with half OB. Stun Removal can shorten it.

entries.name: Derived stat: Empathy Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Empathy Bonus — formula: Basic Stat Bonus Table T-2.1 (p.17) is a piecewise step table this framework's arithmetic-only formulas can't express. Compute your Empathy stat bonus by hand from T-2.1 (plus any racial/special modification) and enter it here.

entries.name: Derived stat: Intuition Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Intuition Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

entries.name: Derived stat: Presence Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Presence Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

entries.name: Derived stat: Quickness Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Quickness Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

entries.name: Derived stat: Strength Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Strength Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

entries.name: Derived stat: Agility Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Agility Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.

entries.name: Derived stat: Constitution Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Constitution Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry. Feeds Exhaustion Points and the Poison/Disease Resistance Rolls.

entries.name: Derived stat: Memory Bonus
entries.content: Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing derived stat. Memory Bonus — formula: Same T-2.1 derivation as Empathy Bonus — see that entry.
